The broad role a Tau fulfills in their society is dictated by the caste to       Tau ground warfare is carried out almost exclusively by the Fire caste,
which they are born, and each caste is physically distinct from one anoth-       while the Air caste is responsible for aerial and void combat, and pro-
er, to the point of being practically separate sub-species.                      viding transport between systems. The basic Fire Caste military unit is
            The Tau of the Fire Caste are the warriors of Tau society, and       known as a Cadre, or "Kau'ui", similar in size and role to an Imperial
are the most massive and physically powerful of the Tau, generations of          Guard Company, and is primarily made up of Tau from the same sept.
breeding having weeded out infirmity.                                                        The most commonly-fielded Cadre is a combined-arms
            Tau of the Earth Caste have the most numerous population             formation (made up of multiple Teams, or La'rua), though more special-
of all the castes, most being physically sturdy laborers who staff farms,        ised Cadres exist such as a Battlesuit Retaliation Cadre and a Pathfinder
factories, and construction crews, and their brightest minds go on to be         Infiltration Cadre. Three to six Cadres will often fight together as part
engineers and doctors.                                                           of a Contingent, or Tio've similar to an Imperial Guard Regiment and
            Tau of the Water Caste are the civil servants, merchants,            commanded by the most senior Cadre commander. Three to six Contin-
administrators, bureaucrats, and diplomats of Tau society, flowing among         gents may be grouped together into a Battle (also known as a Commune
both the other castes and other allied species and ensuring that all have        or Kavaal), though this is only a temporary formation. All Fire Caste
what they need to optimally serve the Greater Good. They display an              forces in a given location, whether a planet or star system, is grouped
easy affinity for languages, and adopt many forms of communications              into a Command under the leadership of a High Commander, with the
with exceptional nuance across their careers.                                    four Commands (or Uash'o) (Fire, Earth, Water and Air) grouped into a
            Tau of the Air Caste are sometimes known as "the invisible           Coalition (or Shan'al) under the command of the local Ethereals.
caste" because they spend most of their time aboard the spacecraft that                      The Tau prefer to carefully plan their assaults and tend to fight
make up the Tau navy. Generations of exposure to micro-gravity leaves            only after carefully coordinating all available troops. They also prefer to
them with hollow bones and a tolerance for high acceleration, though             fight offensively, concerned more with the destruction of the enemy than
their frailty means they are sluggish and weak in even moderate gravity          the taking and holding of ground. The Tau believe that territory is much
environments.                                                                    easier to hold when all enemies are dead. Instead of trying to defend a
            Finally, Tau of the Ethereal Caste are the spiritual and political   base or city, the Tau would rather dismantle all the important technology,
leaders of the Tau, and Tau of other castes submit to their authority in all     evacuate, and come back to defeat the occupying force at a later time
things. Should an Ethereal order a Tau of a different caste to kill them-        when their army is sufficient for the task.
selves, they would be obeyed instantly and without question                                  The two primary Tau tactics (known as metastrategies) are the
                                                                                 Mont'ka (Killing Blow, metastrategy of the perfect strike) and Kauyon
                                                                                 (Patient Hunter, metastrategy of patience and ambush).
                                                                                             The Mont'ka is a carefully planned attack designed to wipe
                                                                                 out critical enemy defenses or units in single, well-placed strikes. Once
                                                                                 the strongest points of enemy resistance are crushed, the remainder of
                                                                                 the force can generally be finished off more easily. Pathfinder Team or
                                                                                 Ghostkeel make the final decision to launch a Mont’ka. After the begin-
                                                                                 ning of the Mont’ka, the enemy must receive massive damage, or else
                                                                                 the Tau forces will be called back – a Commander will withdraw to strike
                                                                                 from another side rather than waste lives of the warriors.
                                                                                             The Kauyon is essentially an ambush, where the enemy is
                                                                                 drawn by use of a "lure" into a carefully prepared killing zones. The lure
                                                                                 can literally be anything - from the allied squad to the vital object. The
                                                                                 force of the Patient Hunter deployed in such a way that they can attack
                                                                                 the enemy using all suitable advantages. True experts of this tactics may
                                                                                 compose so many levels of plans within plans that the enemy realise that
                                                                                 all of his actions have been predicted and managed by the Tau only at the
                                                                                 annihilating ending of its battle.
                                                                                             Aside from these two principles, the Tau also make use of other
                                                                                 metastrategies, including the Rinyon (Circle of Blades, metastrategy
                                                                                 of envelopment) and the Rip'yka (Thousand Daggers, metastrategy of
                                                                                 cumulative strikes).
                                                                                             The Tau have a formidable standing army but also make use
                                                                                 of auxiliary units including the Kroot, Gue'vesa Auxiliaries, and Vespid,
                                                                                 sometimes using them as the lure in the Kauyon attack method




                                                            13.7.0 Forces of the Tau - 1190
                          13.7.1 Warriors of the Tau Empire
The servants of the Tau Empire, in regards to even just the Tau species, are quite varietous. Divided into "castes" these social divisions are not just
that, they are also morphological. These separate castes are the building blocks of Tau society, with the militant Fire Caste forming their armed
forces, the Water Caste being the empire's diplomats and traders, the Earth Caste being labourers, farmers, and technicians, and the Air Caste being
consumate pilots of starships and aircraft all. The capstone of this societal structure is the Ethereal Caste, who lead Tau society from the top, as their

                                              13.7.2 Tau Battlesuits
Battlesuits are used by the Tau and are one of their most advanced pieces of technology. They incorporate many weapons systems and armour com-
parable to a Space Marine's and can easily lay down a withering hail of fire to destroy both infantry and vehicles. These Battlesuits have specific
roles and abilities within the Tau's army. Among the Tau, they are known as "Her'ex'vre", which translates as "Mantle of the Hero". The armour of
Battlesuits is made of dense nanocrystalline alloys which have an impact-resistant structure and consist of a lightweight composition that allows the
suit to carry a great number of weapons and support systems.

                                                                                 allows its user to make Command Tests to Tau Drone, using Tech-Use
                                                                                 in place of the Command Skill. The device can interface with any Drone
                                                                                 within 50 meters , but can only actively issue commands to 2, the others
                                                                                 may report data back to the user, but may not be commanded. A user may
                                                                                 make a Full Action to select a pre-made program to one of his Drones,
                                                                                 granting one of the following abilities:
                                                                                 • Open Fire: +10 Ballistic Skill, Unnatural Ballistic Skill (+2)
                                                                                 • Evade: +10 Dodge, Step Aside
                                                                                 • Survey: +10 Perception, +10 Awareness, Keen Intuition
                                                                                 • Seek: +10 Perception, +10 Survival, Surefoot Wayfinder
                                                                                 • Pursue: Unnatural Agility (+2), Accustomed To Crowds

                                                                                 Early Warning Override
                                                                                 Similar in construction and use to the counterfire defence system, the
                                                                                 early warning override tracks fast moving vehicles and relays the posi-
                                                                                 tional data to the user. This allows for accurate prediction of flight paths
                                                                                 and other movement vectors. The override is also calibrated to detect the
                                                                                 electronic disturbance caused by teleporter devices.
                                                                                            Once per Encounter, a Tau using a battlesuit with this Support
                                                                                 System may make an Overwatch Action as a Reaction.

Stabilization Systems
The weapons that can be brought to bear by Tau battlesuits are enormous
and terrible, but they can be unwieldy in the extreme. To account for this
some battlesuits integrate advanced gyroscopic and tracking systems
along with servo-stabilizers that allow them to be wielded far more
easily.
           The battlesuit gains the Auto-Stabilized Trait.

Stimulant Injector
A stimulant injector allows its user to inject a series of medical and com-
bat stimms without having to stop fighting, or fumble in a medi-kit.
            Once per Round as an any-time Free Action, a Tau in a bat-
tlesuit with this Support System may inject a single dose of the loaded
drug into his system. The injector can carry up to six doses of one or
more drug. If the injector is loaded with more than one type of drug, the
character may choose which drug is applied in any order.
            The usual drug employed by the Tau Empire is a pain suppres-
sant, to allow a warrior to fight beyond his usual limits. A dose of this
drug allows the imbiber to ignore a single Critical Effect he is suffering
until the end of the encounter, so long as this effect would not kill him
outright.

Shield Generator
Often found affixed to battlesuits or drones, a Tau shield generator works
something like an Imperial refractor field. The generator projects a wave
of energy designed to intercept incoming projectiles and forces, redirect-
ing them away from the projector or robbing them of all kinetic energy.
          A Tau using a battlesuit equipped with this Support System
gains a Force Field with a Protection Rating of 40 and Overload of 05.

Target Lock System
Many battlesuits pilots fit their suits with target lock systems, sophisti-
cated sets of sensors and arrays that allow the pilot to instantly identify
threats and eliminate them with his battlesuit’s considerable firepower.
           A Tau using a battlesuit with a Target Lock System does not
lose the benefit of an Aim Action when he makes a Reaction.

                           13.7.2 Tau Battlesuits - 1201
                                                      13.7.3 Tau Drones
The Tau make use of a staggering range of artificial intelligences, a fact that damns the entire race in the eyes of the Adeptus Mechanicus and much
of the Imperial hierarchy. Such intelligences that have been imbued into a mobile device are reffered to as Drones, and these can take many different
forms. Some Drones are able to interact with their masters, obeying simple instructions and even anticipating what duties are required of them. The
Tau appear to value these Drone intelligences, and while they are not regarded as having an equal status to a Tau, they ar etreated with a degree of
respect, perhaps akin to a favoured animal companion. Drones are disk-shaped machines that move around by way of a small anti-gravatic generator
and are fitted with tools or weapons according to thier station. While some Drones serve individual masters they are most deadly when operating in a
larger, independent squadron. When operating in such a capacity, the Gun Drones are able to network their processing, targeting, and sensor systems
together, making the whole far more effective than the sum of their parts.

                                                                       13.7.3 Tau Drones - 1204
                                              13.7.4 Tau Auxiliaries
The Tau Empire incorporates various other xeno species into its fold, with the nature of the relations between the Tau and these assimilated races
ranging from that of favoured and well-trusted allies to little more than enslavement. The Tau are ultimately an integrationalist empire and one
that finds use for its subjects, one way or another. For the better favoured xenos that serve the Greater Good it is far from uncommon to see them
fighting alongside the Tau on the field of battle, with Kroot being a common sight on the periphery of Tau armed forces, when the conditions for
mutual benefit arise. More uncommon yet, the insectoid Vespids are another, more common auxiliary force, with their natural abilities lending to
them being effective scouts and skirmishers.

                                                                 13.7.4 Tau Auxiliaries - 1208
                              13.7.5 War Machines of the Tau
The vehicles of the Tau are much like the rest of their wargear, advanced, sophisticated, and well-made. Despite their heretical aspect the inclusion
of drone-operated weapons systems increases the combat effectiveness of these vehicles, and their plasma thrust engiens couple with anti-gravity
systems make them all dangerously maneuverable and swift. These vehicles are light for their size, and while their armour is impressively durable
for it's seemingly negligible thickness, the Tau's war machines largely rely on speed, ambush, and the ability to escape easily for their defense far
more than the durability of their hulls. Complimenting this is the weapons systems these vehicles bring to bear, many of them utilizing pulse-based
plasma technology, missile systems, and even linear acceleration weaponry that pierce even void shields.
           The Fire Caste Pilot profile should be used for the Pilot, Co-Pilot, and Gunner roles for all Tetra, Pirahna, Devilfish, Hammerhead, and
Sky Ray vehicles, where as the Air Caste Pilot profile should be used for the Pilot, Co-Pilot, Gunner, Bombardier, and Commander roles for all
Razorshark, Sunshark, Barracuda, Tiger Shark, Orca, and Manta vehicles.

                                   13.8.0 Forces of the Tyranids
The Tyranids, also known as The Great Devourer are an extragalactic alien race, whose sole purpose is the consumption of all forms of genetic and
biological material in order to evolve and reproduce. Tyranid technology is based entirely on biological engineering. Every function is carried out
by living, engineered creatures, each of which collectively forms the Hive Fleet, directed by a single Hive Mind.
          The Tyranids are one of the gravest threats to the entire galaxy. They seek only to consume all organic life and cannot be reasoned with or
deterred in this quest. Worse still for all organic life, thus far the Tyranid Hive Fleets that have been encountered are hypothesized to be merely the
furthest stretched tendril of a main invasion fleet that is still traveling in the void of space.

                                                         13.8.0 Forces of the Tyranids - 1220
                                        13.8.1 Genestealer Cultists
Genestealer Cults form if a Genestealer infects members of another species with its genotype. The resultant changes in the genome of the host cause
a fanatical loyalty to the Genestealers as well as a drastic change to their reproductive system; their firstborn children will be Hybrids, a grotesque
mixture of the host's race and Genestealers. These hybrids infect further victims, and the infection spreads exponentially. Fourth generation hybrids
produce Purestrain Genestealers, and the cycle starts once again. This brood of Purestrains, hybrids and Brood Brothers is held together by strong
psychic and genetic bonds, and assembles around the original Genestealer which becomes the Patriarch. Because this community is often hidden
behind the facade of a religion or political movement, it is called a Genestealer Cult by the Imperium.
          As the cult's numbers grow, more specialized types of Genestealer Hybrids are created to serve the Patriarch, which is now worshiped as
a god. These include Maguses, Primuses, Locuses, etc.. The Cult will often grow and plot below the surface of their host world, using this base of
operations to gradually infiltrate into the above society. Later generations are less monstrous than their forbears and can freely walk among Imperial
society without much notice. Often a Genestealer Cult will recruit from the downtrodden and underbelly of society, characterizing themselves as
liberators from the brutal yoke of Imperial rule. A fully mature Cult can be huge, numbering in the billions and covering several worlds.
          The Cult's primary concern is their propagation, but overtime this transitions to preparing their host world for the coming of a Tyranid
Hive Fleet. Cultists often see this as an anointed holy day of salvation, and they will work fanatically to see a victim population is ready for con-
sumption. At the chosen hour the Geneestealer Cult rises up, unleashing a devastating and well-planned assault that can devastate entire systems.

taint, or perhaps even in the case of a Rogue Trader or other great house                  Restrictions: None, though it is unlikely for Genestealer
of nobility being corrupted, the GM is more than warranted to have the          Cultists to be capable of hijacking something as prominent as a cruiser or
cult be armed with both rarer and heavier weapons than those listed in          battlecruiser.
their profiles, perhaps with commensurately better armour and a wider                      Modifications: Add +10 to the ship's Crew Rating. Change the
variety of useful tools as well.                                                Crew Quarters to be a Clan-Kin Quarters Component.
            As for vehicles, genestealer cults have a tendency of using mil-               Additions: The ship's crew always gain an extra 1d5-1 extra
itary vehicles where available (usually acquired by corrupting the local        Degrees of Success on Boarding Actions and Raid Actions.
PDF forces), but will often enough convert civilian vehicles for mili-
tary use. This can involve any number of modifications, with common
ones being the installation of extra armour and weapons on non-combat
vehicles. When the cult deigns to reveal itself these vehicles will often
be bedecked in the colours and iconography of the cult, but largely they
are kept quietly maintained in hidden garages, away from prying eyes, or
else used in their standard capacity.
            Though the GM is well within their limits to allow the mem-
bers of a Genestealer cult to use vehicles largely reserved for the Imperial
Guard and Imperial Navy, it will generally be far more common to find
vehicles from Section 7.2 "Civilian Vehicles" with added weapons,
armour, or simply just well-armed passengers.

                                                                  13.8.1 Genestealer Cultists - 1227
                            13.8.2 Tyranid Synapse Creatures
Stalking amidst the throng of xenos chattel come fearsome creatures, far more terrifying than their single-minded kin. Bipedal warrior-forms and
towering abominations advance, a singular, hateful intellect burning behind their beady eyes. These are the agents of the Hive Mind, who direct the
deadly flow of the invasion swarms with lethal cunning.

                     Synaptic Lynchpins                                                    Neurothrope: Occasionally the Hive Mind will seed alpha
           Hive Tyrant: Hive Tyrants are the commanders of the Tyranid          beasts known as Neurothropes amidst clusters of Zoanthropes. These
swarms and enact the Hive Mind’s will on the field of battle. Though            fell creatures possess the power to leech the very life force from their
individuals display a wide variety of physical characteristics, all Hive Ty-    foes, mending their wounds even as the wizened cadaver of their victim
rants are fearsome hulking monsters that tower over even a Dreadnought.         topples to the floor. Neurothropes can also use their parasitic power to
They are brutally strong, able to shatter ferrocrete with sickening ease.       heal nearby Zoanthropes, which helps to safeguard against the overload
Every part of such a beast’s body is perfectly created to kill, even the        of psychic energy that commonly overwhelms these creatures.
layers of chitinous plating that protect them. A Hive Tyrant is a formida-      ided in the destruction of countless worlds, and slaughtered foes of all
ble opponent at any distance, as deadly with ranged weapons as it is with       descriptions. They direct the bio-weapon fire of nearby Tyranid Warriors
bonesword or claw.                                                              with unerring precision.
           Tyrant Guard: Warriors who attempt to slay a Tyranid lead-                      Maleceptor: The Maleceptor is the purest embodiment of the

with huge, scything blades and crushing claws. There is no way past this        that rules the Tyranid race. As it advances ominously into battle, warp
deadly obstacle, and those who approach are clubbed to death or hacked          energy spears from its eyeless cranium, vapourising all in its path. Those

                               13.8.3 Powers of the Hive Mind
Many Tyranid bio-forms possess potent psychic powers, manifested not from drawing the power of the warp but by tapping into the vast gestalt will
of the Hive Mind itself. Such is the potency of the Hive Mind that a fully fledged Tyranid fleet can blanket entire regions of space with its presence,
casting a shadow in the warp and projecting its ancient and terrifying consciousness across the barrier between Materium and Immaterium. When
a Tyranid creature with a particularly strong connection to the Hive Mind, or the ability to channel its power, taps into this vast store of will, it can
create deadly psychic effects, subverting minds, incinerating flesh or even bending reality to aid the Tyranids’ all consuming hunger.
          Tyranid creatures with a Psy Rating, such as a Hive Tyrant or Zoanthrope, follow all the normal rules for Bound Psykers with the excep-
tions that if a Tyranid psychic creature suffers a Psychic Phenomena or Perils of the Warp, it does not roll on either table. Instead it suffers 2d10
True Energy Damage, as it loses control of the power and the immense strength of the Hive Mind backlashes upon it; otherwise, the power has no
effect.

Termagants and Hormagaunts are simple bioforms created by the hive fleets in their billions. Onslaughts by these creatures often precede the main
attack, wave after wave hurling themselves against enemy lines like an avalanche of teeth, claws and bio-weapons fire.

                   The Endless Swarms                                                    Hormagaunt: The Hormagaunt is a highly specialised iter-

by the hive fleets, each Ripper is little more than an armoured serpent,      single spore’s worth of Hormagaunts reaches the surface it can swiftly
terminating in a broad maw crammed with needle-sharp teeth. They are          develop into a serious problem for the prey world’s defenders. From the
persistent, and quite capable of pulling down creatures many times their      moment they have landed, the Hormagaunts rove the landscape in sweep-

ferocious feeding instincts.                                                  until it has run its quarry down and torn it apart with frenzied strikes of
           Termagant: Termagants are fast, agile and cunning creatures.       its scythe-like forelimbs. Upon making a kill, a Hormagaunt will hungri-
They are amongst the smallest of the Hive Mind’s warriors, little more        ly feed upon its prey’s remains, tearing hunks of bloody flesh from the
than two metres from head to tail, having originally been created to roam     slaughtered corpse with razor-sharp teeth. Such a gruesome feast seldom
the arterial passages of bio-ships in search of intruders. In planetary       lasts long, for the Hormagaunt’s hyper-accelerated metabolism drives it

on four legs whilst unleashing torrents of fire from the anti-personnel

forelimbs.
           Of course, there are times when a Tyranid assault requires that
Termagants are thrown directly at the foe’s lines, forcing the defenders to
expend vast amounts of ammunition to hold back a tide of alien bodies.
Thisis far from an exceptional tactic; it is simply part of the Termagants’
role. On such occasions the Hive Mind simply suppresses the Terma-
gants’ survival instincts and sends them forward to die in droves until
ammo stores are depleted and victory is assured.
           A Termagant’s mind is vicious but simplistic, and if separated
from the Hive Mind’s influence is apt to become confused. On such occa-
sions the creature’s self-preservation instincts take over, and it abandons
the fight in search of shelter. So it is that an army that has driven off a
Tyranid assault must proceed with great care. Every shadowed cave, tum-
bled ruin or patch of tangled undergrowth could conceal a nest of fugitive
Termagants that will fight with incredible determination upon discovery.

                       13.8.5 Tyranid Vanguard Organisms
Crawling forth from the dark corners of the Imperium come lithe and powerful forms, razor-sharp claws gleaming in the twilight, predatory eyes
filled with lethal cunning. These are the vanguard organisms of the Tyranids, sent ahead of the hive fleets to slaughter and subvert, paving the way
for the devastation of entire sectors.

            Genestealers: There are many terrifying creatures in the                     Lictor: The Lictor is a highly specialised development of
Tyranid hive fleets, but one in particular has carved out a horrifying and    the Tyranid Warrior bioform, specifically adapted to fill a scout role in
bloody legend on more than a thousand worlds. It is a lurker in dark plac-    the vanguard of the Tyranid advance. Lictors rove ahead of the main
es, a clawed harbinger of sudden death. It is known as the Genestealer,       body of a swarm, seeking out pockets of resistance to be eradicated
and it is a plague upon the galaxy.                                           and native life forms to be absorbed. Able to move swiftly and without
            A Genestealer is a swift and powerful predator with light-        sound through even the densest terrain, and concealed by a Cameleonic
ning-fast reflexes and serrated claws that can tear through the thickest of   carapace that renders it all but invisible to the naked eye, a Lictor can
armour. Genestealers also have large, highly adaptive brains and possess      remain hidden until it chooses to strike. It can wait motionless for days,
a form of brood telepathy that allows them to function independently          unnoticed by its victims, an unseen herald of approaching disaster.
from the Hive Mind. This autonomy allows them to destroy through                         Lictors are not instinctively aggressive, as they are created
stealth and guile that which cannot be defeated through numbers alone.        primarily to locate prey for the wider swarm. Lictors are opportunistic
The mightiest of these creatures are the Broodlords, hulking killers which    hunters and therefore tend to stalk their quarry from the shadows, avoid-
lead the Genestealers in their bloody ambushes.                               ing confrontations where they would be vastly outmatched. A Lictor will
            A strong survival instinct drives Genestealers outwards from      often pick off its prey in ones and twos whilst they are separated from
the hive fleets, and they seek out space-bound vessels attempting to flee     their comrades, sometimes retreating for days at a time before launching
the surface of doomed prey worlds. It is simple for a Genestealer to sto      a further attack.
away aboard such ships, nesting unseen amongst crawl spaces until it is                  When the time comes to strike, Lictors are brutally effi-
brought to a new planet by the unsuspecting crew. If a single Genestealer     cient,with a whole arsenal of bio-weaponry that includes mantis-like
reaches an inhabited world, it can spell disaster. Genestealers reproduce     claws, talons that can pierce steel, barbed flesh hooks and feeder tendrils.
by implanting other life forms with their own genetic material. Once          The feeder tendrils are tipped with sharpened bony plates that can pierce
infected, a victim is enthralled by the Genestealers’ nascent telepathy       a victim’s skull as easily as they poke through eyeballs and the sockets
and Tyranid attributes are passed on to its offspring, creating monstrous     behind. They are used to lobotomise victims so that the Lictor can swiftly
hybrids completely under the alien’s domination. These deformities            devour its brain and absorb its memories. Thus, in death, the enemy re-
eventually breed true, creating Purestrain Genestealers under the control     veals more to a Lictor than it ever did in life, betraying the whereabouts
of the progenitor of the cult, the Genestealer Patriarch – a formidably       of comrades and exposing any weaknesses that might be exploited.
intelligent alpha beast possessing fearsome telepathic power. For years                  Yet fearsome as the Lictor is as a physical foe, it has an alto-
these creatures lurk in sewers and caves beneath cities, preying on the       gether more deadly purpose than simple slaughter. Stalking Lictors exude
populace like folk-tale monsters. Within just a few years they will have      a pheromone trail which draws other Tyranids; the larger the concen-
assembled a vast network of mind-controlled operatives, embedded              tration of prey, the stronger the response and the more irresistible the
in every stratum of the local planetary government and military. Thus         lure. So it is that even killing a Lictor is no guarantee of survival, for the
placed they wait, sometimes for many years, until the Hive Mind’s will        creature’s mere presence ensures that the swarm already knows where its
once again dominates their psyches.                                           prey can be found. After that, it’s only a matter of time…
            No one knows how widespread the Genestealer infestation has
become or how many worlds if affects. For every brood uncovered
and purged, a dozen go unnoticed. When a Tyranid hive fleet enters an
infested system, the Hive Mind asserts its synaptic dominion over the
Broodlord and its clan. Planetary defenders are thrown into disarray as
Genestealers suddenly burst from the shadows, overwhelming crucial
systems and leaving the prey world vulnerable before the merciless
Tyranid onslaught.

                  13.8.6 Tyranid Subterranean Organisms
When faced with a fortified enemy position, the Hive Mind will deploy burrowing organisms – blade-limbed horrors that burst from the earth in
the midst of the defenders and carve their terrified prey to bloody chunks. Some of these monsters stand as tall as buildings, and are able to peel the
armour from a tank with sickening ease.

                     Death From Below                                                    Trygon: TheTrygon is a vast serpentine creature, so colossal
            Ravener: Raveners are voracious predators, their clawed           that it towers over even the mighty Carnifex. It is a heavily armoured
and snake-like bodies driven onwards by an all-consuming hunger that          monster, covered from head to tail with a thick carapace of shifting
is remarkable even amongst their predatory race. Twisted musculature          plates. As the Trygon moves, these plates generate a potent bio-static
grants these beasts a terrifying turn of speed. Raveners can bound over       charge that courses along the length of the beast’s body and wreathes its
small obstacles in an eyeblink, dart between larger obstructions and even     bladed forelimbs with crackling power. TheTrygon can direct this energy
slither through flooded marshland with bewildering swiftness. Yet such is     as a lethal high-voltage discharge – unleashing pulsing arcs of lightning
not the Raveners’ only form of approach and neither is it the most feared,    that leave its prey as little more than a charred pile of scorched bones.
for at least when these alien horrors are charging their prey down across                A Trygon’s claws are not only fearsome in close combat, they
the battlefield, the enemy has a chance to see their doom. The power          also allow it to burrow through practically any material. When a Trygon
housed within the Raveners’ wiry forms allows them to burrow long             detects an enemy above, it digs upwards, bursting through the ground
distances beneath a world’s surface, before emerging in a spray of earth      with explosive force, its huge blade-limbs scything through warriors and
right in front of an enemy position, claws eviscerating their ambushed        tanks alike. Such subterranean attacks are hard to detect and harder to
prey whilst their thoraxmounted weapon symbiotes spit death.                  defend against, especially on worlds with background seismic activity.
            Mawloc: Mawlocs are huge worm-like creatures with great           Once the beast emerges, only focused heavy-weapons fire can be relied
distended jaws. They are the tunnelling outriders to the Tyranid swarm,       upon to bring it down, for the Trygon’s iron-hard carapace is proof
and burrow deep beneath the ground to bypass a prey world’s front-            against all else.
line defences. Once past the outer perimeter, a Mawloc bursts forth in a                 Trygons excavate a massive network of underground tunnels as
shower of dirt and stone, swallowing any foes unfortunate enough to be        they burrow beneath the surface of a prey world. Other Tyranid creatures
standing where it emerges. The Mawloc then runs rampant among the             use the passageways left in the Trygon’s wake, scuttling unseen as battle
reeling enemy, wreaking as much havoc and carnage as it can with its          rages overhead. The emergence of a tunnelling Trygon therefore often
overmuscled tail before vanishing back below ground once more. Severe         heralds a larger Tyranid attack, with hordes of creatures pouring out of
tremors are the only warning of a Mawloc attack, making sentry duty on        the tunnel shortly after its emergence.
a seismically active world a particularly harrowing experience for the                   Trygon Prime: As with many Tyranid organisms, differ-
defenders should a hive fleet enter the system.                               ent Trygons display substantial variety; one of the most distinct is the
            Physically, a Mawloc is an incredibly simple Tyranid bioform,     Trygon Prime. These beasts have elongated jaws and containment spines
with little concession given to other roles. Its six clawed limbs are com-    running the length of their sinuous bodies, to better harness and direct
paratively small and whilst they lack the reach to be especially efficient    their bio-electric discharges. More dangerous still, these Trygons share a
in combat, they are nonetheless incredibly powerful, employed to gain         strong synaptic link with the Hive Mind and are able to dominate the will
extra traction whilst burrowing and haul the Mawloc through its tunnels.      of lesser Tyranid creatures.
This should not be taken to mean a Mawloc is defenceless; nothing could
be further from the truth. A Mawloc’s massive, razortoothed maw is the
entryway to an equally cavernous gullet. Most of the creature’s victims
are swallowed whole, there to be painfully digested over the course of
several days. Should an item of prey prove large enough to stick in the
Mawloc’s craw, they are first pounded flat by a battery of blows from the
creature’s muscular tail before being devoured.
            A Mawloc is almost entirely blind, and relies on information
provided by a series of pressure-sensitive organs that run the length of
its flanks. These can absorb and decipher pressure waves, creating a ma-
ny-layered picture of the world around the Mawloc. It is this ability that
allows the creature to hunt its prey even whilst burrowing through the
ground. Even the slightest tremor above ground grants a hunting Mawloc
a wealth of information, enabling it to intercept a quarry with frightening
speed and unerring accuracy. The more regular and rhythmic the sound,
the more likely it is that a Mawloc will be able to home in on the source.
The pounding thump of a terrified heartbeat is like a flaring beacon to a
Mawloc. Thusit is a victim’s own fear that betrays their whereabouts and
brings about their destruction.

As a Tyranid invasion progresses, the clouds of spores that choke the prey world’s skies become thicker and thicker. The slow darkening of a prey
world’s skies is an omen of its impending doom, as unthinkable quantities of Tyranid spores are spewed into its atmosphere. Some of these are
microscopic in size, and drift along in great clouds, wreaking disaster upon the planet’s ecology. Others are bloated, chitin-plated things, their fleshy
bulk packed with dormant organisms or explosive gases. These cloying particles are expelled in their billions by specialised bioforms – sporecaster
organisms that ravage their foes with suffocating toxic miasmas, flesh-melting acids and predatory, semi-sentient viruses.

destroying its foes from a great distance. These ‘living artillery’ bioforms are not only powerful weapons in the Hive Mind’s arsenal, but proof of
the Tyranids’ highly adaptive nature.

            Hive Guard have an incredibly short incubation cycle and can
be maintained as end-stage larvae almost indefinitely. This means that
rather than wasting precious biomass by creating and sustaining protec-
tors that will stand idle, the Hive Mind can swiftly spawn Hive Guard
wherever its advance is threatened, meeting an enemy counter-attack
with salvo after salvo of intense firepower. Those few warriors who have
launched a strike at the heart of a Tyranid bio-ship and returned alive
report being suddenly surrounded by scores of these guardian organisms,
spawned forth in haste by the vessel to defend its vital organs.

                        13.8.9 Tyranid Monstrous Creatures
The Hive Mind creates an unending cavalcade of specialized and horrific creatures, each one suited to its terrible task involved in the consumption
of worlds. These monstrous creatures are not only deadly but horrifically enduring, able to endure withering storms of heavy weapons fire.

            Dimachaeron: The Dimachaeron appears to have evolved for
a single purpose: to slaughter those identified among their prey as leaders
in the midst of battle, spreading terror and dismay among the ranks of all
who resist the Hive Mind's advance. Bristling with blade-arms studded
with sickle-like claws, it can slice a fully armoured Space Marine in two
and is able to leap a Leman Russ Battle Tank without breaking stride.
When stalking its prey the Dimachaeron dispenses with the slow, stealthy
approach of the Lictor and instead relies on sheer brutality and animalis-
tic rage, leaving a gore-soaked trail of carnage behind it.
            Perhaps even more fearsome than the array of sickle claws,
razor-sharp teeth and tail spikes is the spine-ringed maw hidden within
the Dimachaeron's thorax. Any foe unfortunate enough to be caught in
the beast's grasp will be held in place while the thorax hinges open and
the fanged maw impales them. While the trap-like jaws of the Dimachae-
ron's ribcage hold the victim in place, the spine-maw injects them with a
potent bio-acid, reducing their internal organs to a slurry of nutrients that
are then absorbed by the Tyranid to bolster its own physiology, allowing
it to ignore all but the most horrific of injuries.

                                                           13.8.9 Tyranid Monstrous Creatures - 1248
                                     13.8.10 Tyranid Skyswarms
Tyranid bioforms sweep across the sky in leather-winged clouds, casting flickering shadows across the terrified troops below. With a chorus of
unnatural shrieks, they fold their wings and dive towards their prey, spitting caustic acid that scorches and blinding. Amidst the flock larger shapes
